artworks.title: Zeus and Porphyrion (Pergamon Altar, east frieze)
artworks.description: On the east frieze of the Great Altar of Pergamon, Zeus storms against the Giant identified as Porphyrion — the greatest of the earthborn beside Alcyoneus. Hellenistic marble makes the king of the Giants the thunderer's chief antagonist in the Gigantomachy.

artworks.title: Zeus group, Pergamon Altar
artworks.description: Another view of the Zeus combat on the Pergamon frieze: eagle, thunderbolt, and falling Giants — the sculptural stage on which Porphyrion's assault on Hera and Zeus was carved for the Attalid capital.

artworks.title: Zeus against Porphyrion (Pergamon Altar)
artworks.description: A closer photograph titles the duel: Zeus contra Porphyrion on the Great Altar now in Berlin. Apollodorus makes this Giant lust for Hera until Zeus blasts him; the frieze turns that lore into stone combat.

artworks.title: Pergamon Zeus (Gigantomachy detail)
artworks.description: Detail of Zeus in the Gigantomachy frieze — the god who, with Heracles' aid, ends Porphyrion's assault. The Pergamon Altar remains the defining public image of the Giant who challenged Olympus.

popCulture.title: Pergamon Altar
popCulture.description: The Great Altar's Gigantomachy frieze stages Zeus against Porphyrion — the earthborn king of the Giants carved for Pergamon and now in Berlin.

popCulture.title: Porphyrion
popCulture.description: Greatest of the Giants with Alcyoneus — Apollodorus' attacker of Hera, slain by Zeus' thunderbolt and Heracles' arrows in the Gigantomachy.
